title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 28 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 28)

content.overview: Section 28 distinguishes international commercial arbitration from other arbitrations. In international commercial arbitration, parties may designate the substantive law and, absent designation, the tribunal applies appropriate rules of law. In other arbitrations, the tribunal applies the substantive law in force in India. The tribunal must also decide in accordance with the contract and applicable trade usages.

content.study:
Section 28 — Rules applicable to substance of dispute

Section 28 distinguishes international commercial arbitration from other arbitrations. In international commercial arbitration, parties may designate the substantive law and, absent designation, the tribunal applies appropriate rules of law. In other arbitrations, the tribunal applies the substantive law in force in India. The tribunal must also decide in accordance with the contract and applicable trade usages.

Apply the provision by identifying operative conditions, exceptions, procedural stage and connected provisions. Do not substitute generic arbitration practice for the statutory rule.
